reference.name: Royal Botanic Gardens, Peradeniya

sources.quote: Royal Botanic Gardens, Peradeniya are about 5.5 km to the west of the city of Kandy in the Central Province of Sri Lanka.

reference.rationale: Kandy day pairing the Temple of the Tooth with the Royal Botanical Garden = Royal Botanic Gardens, Peradeniya (A and B agree).

variants.name: ok
variants.rationale: Official name, Peradeniya, Central Province, Sri Lanka all match the reference.

facts.rationale: Both unverifiable (official site only says the Java fig on the Great Lawn spreads 'like a giant living umbrella'; roots/most-photographed claims unsourced). trip_leak resolved true: 'one of the most photographed trees' describes what visitors do/see.

sources.quote: There are over 200 species of palms in the Gardens.
The bamboo collection is along River Drive to the right of the Lake.

facts.rationale: Official site documents palm and bamboo collections; orchids are its best-known collection (Wikipedia).

sources.quote: Later, in the reign of King Kirti Sri from 1747 to 1780 this was made a Royal Garden

facts.rationale: Official history: made a Royal Garden under Kandyan king Kirti Sri (1747-1780).

sources.quote: There are avenues in the River Drive such as Cook's Pine Avenue, Palmyra Palm Avenue, Double Coconut Avenue, Cabbage Palm Avenue, and Royal Palm Avenue.
The garden includes more than 4000 species of plants, including orchids, spices, medicinal plants and palm trees.

facts.rationale: Palm avenues, orchids, spices, medicinal plants all documented.

sources.quote: Extent: 147 acres (59 hectares).
The area 61.25 ha in extent, is about 1550ft from sea level.

facts.rationale: 147 acres = 59 ha (official 59-61.25 ha); "about 60 hectares" within tolerance.

sources.quote: The Royal Botanic Gardens at Peradeniya was established in 1821, six years after the final occupation of the Kandyan Kingdom by the English.
In the early years work was mainly directed towards the introduction and acclimatization of useful and ornamental plants

facts.rationale: Established 1821 under the British; early work on introducing useful/economic plants.

sources.quote: Royal Botanic Gardens, Peradeniya are about 5.5 km to the west of the city of Kandy in the Central Province of Sri Lanka.

facts.rationale: Basic identity statement.

sources.quote: the Botanic Garden was used by Lord Louis Mountbatten, the supreme commander of the allied forces in the South Asia, as the headquarters of the South East Asia Command
SEAC headquarters moved in April 1944 to Kandy in Ceylon.

facts.rationale: Both supported; numeric resolved true because the fact states a year (1944). Deciding sources: Wikipedia garden article + SEAC article (April 1944 move to Kandy), both quotes checked on the raw pages.

sources.quote: Extent: 147 acres (59 hectares).
occupies a loop of the river Mahaweli, which surrounds it on all sides except the south

facts.rationale: About 59-61 ha, on a loop of the Mahaweli.

The Royal Botanic Gardens at Peradeniya was established in 1821, six years after the final occupation of the Kandyan Kingdom by the English.

facts.rationale: Royal Garden of Kandyan kings, then established 1821 under the British (official site; Wikipedia gives 1843 as formal establishment, but the official body says 1821).

It is near the Mahaweli River (the longest river in Sri Lanka).

facts.rationale: Near Kandy and beside the Mahaweli.

sources.quote: Considered Sri Lanka’s largest botanical garden, with 147 acres and over 4000 species of plants, Peradeniya Botanical Garden is a well-known attraction in Sri Lanka
It is renowned for its collection of orchids. The garden includes more than 4000 species of plants, including orchids, spices, medicinal plants and palm trees.

facts.rationale: A supported vs B unverifiable (superlative). Resolved supported: Time Out (T2, no T1 contrary) calls it Sri Lanka's largest botanical garden and a well-known attraction; Wikipedia/official site give 1.6 million visitors (2016) and the orchid/palm/spice collections. 'Best-known' is a mild, sourced superlative.

facts.rationale: River loop surrounding all sides except south = peninsula in a river bend; near Kandy.

147 acres and 4000+ species (palms, orchids, spices, medicinal plants) are supported, but 'one of Asia's largest collections of labelled trees' has no reliable source.

sources.quote: The history of the Royal Botanic Gardens dates as far back as 1371 when King Wickramabahu iii ascended the throne and kept court at Peradeniya
It was founded in the late 15th century and endured until the early 19th century.

facts.rationale: A contradicted vs B supported. Resolved contradicted: the official site dates the 1371 link to King Wickramabahu III keeping court (a Gampola-era king) and says the site was 'made a Royal Garden' only under Kirti Sri (1747-1780); the Kandyan kingdom itself dates from the late 15th century (Wikipedia), so a 14th-century pleasure garden 'of the Kandyan kings' is false.
